raw_response:
I am a small farmer, only 4.1 mu, so I cannot take big risks. My land has been wheat-maize for many years, and I will still do it this way this year. Wheat and maize both matter to me. If one side is not good, maybe the other side can still give some grain and money. I do mostly what worked before. I do not read those technical things, I look at the field, the weather, and what people around me do.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, after the weather turns cooler. I will use the seed people nearby usually buy, not the expensive kind. Before sowing, I will put fertilizer once as base fertilizer, not too little because wheat needs a strong start, but not too much because fertilizer costs cash. If the wheat苗 looks weak or yellow after winter, I will topdress once more around jointing. Water is from the well, but pumping costs money, so I will probably irrigate about 3 times for wheat: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once around overwintering or greening, and once around jointing or grain filling depending on rain. For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. That time is rushed, so I will not do fancy tillage. I will clear the wheat and plant maize quickly, with simple shallow tillage or direct seeding if I can arrange it. Maize grows fast in summer, so if there is enough rain I save on irrigation, but if it is dry around tasseling I will water once or twice. I will use some fertilizer, mainly before or at planting, and maybe a little more later if the crop looks weak. I do not like cutting fertilizer too much because if yield drops, that hurts more than spending a bit extra.
